ORDER Heard Sri. Srinand A. Pachhapure, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Praveena Y.
Devareddiyavara, learned HCGP for the respondent No.1-State.

Sri. Kishor S. Sutar and Sri.
Neelendra D. Gunde, learned counsels for respondent No.2.
2.

The petitioner is before this Court seeking regular bail in Crime No.54/2024 of respondent Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 376(2)(f), 376(2)(I) and 506 r/w 34 of IPC.

Brief facts of the case:
3.
It is the case of the prosecution that Smt. Mallavva W/o Somanna Gavade lodged a complaint stating that they are the shepherds and having 200 sheep.
It is further stated that her younger brother had 300 sheep and it was being looked after by Parashuram who is the petitioner herein.
The daughter of the complainant NC: 2024:KHC-D:9743 studied upto 9th standard and left the school thereafter and was staying at home.
4. On 06.03.2024 around 6.00 a.m., the complainant had been to land to bring the fodder to the sheep and her husband had gone to bring firewood.
The victim went to attend her nature call near the house and came back by crying.

When the complainant enquired as to what happened to her,
she disclosed that the said Parashuram committed sexual assault when she had been to attend the nature call, and ran away from the spot after she raised hue and cry and also after seeing her father.
Based on the statement of complainant, a complaint came to be registered against the petitioner and another.
After conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
5. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was working along with the younger brother of the complainant.
The petitioner was taking care of the sheep along with her younger brother.
There was a rift between younger brother of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:9743 complainant and the petitioner in respect of wages.

The complainant filed a false complaint against Sri Manjunath S/O. Shivappa Koulapuri vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39099907/
2 the petitioner in order to throw him away from the work.

sentences.text:
6. It is further submitted that the victim had informed her mother that prior to the alleged incident,
she has been subjected to sexual intercourse with Manjunath who is arraigned as accused No.1 two years ago from the date of the alleged incident.
However, she did not inform the said act to her parents, that itself indicates that she was matured enough to understand the consequences.
Therefore, the bail application of the petitioner may be considered and he may be enlarged on bail.
7. Per contra, learned HCGP vehemently opposed the said contentions and submitted that the act of the petitioner has been immediately resisted by way of lodging the complaint.
The father of the victim had witnessed the incident.
The age of the victim is 15 years and 5 months as on the date of the incident.
Therefore, it is not appropriate to grant bail.

After having considered the submissions of the learned counsels of the respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet and also statement of the victim, it appears from the record that the victim had been subjected to rape by the petitioner on 03.02.2024 around 7.30 a.m.
9.
In the said complaint, it is also stated that the same victim had been subjected to sexual assault two years ago as on the date of lodging the complaint.
However, it was not brought to the notice of her parents.

10. The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that even though the petitioner had not committed any offence, he has been falsely implicated in this case only in order to avoid the wages payable to the petitioner may be accepted.

11. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:9743 ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.54/2024 of respondent Police Station, on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court,
subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court till disposal of the case.
c) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
